why: The launcher layer was written against a layout that no longer exists: WORMZ/, HYDRA/, HORUS/, METAWORMS/, scripts/, ml_platforms/ and the three UTILITIES kernels sat at the repo root, and $PERSEPHONE_ROOT pointed at a copy with bin/ inside it. Each entry below is measured, not guessed -- every one was a tail or basename match in a 2026-10-31 census, and declaring it upgrades that match from inference to fact. At most one directory level has moved per entry, so the mapping is the layout change itself rather than a list of 67 files. A declaration that matches no reference is reported as stale_alias, so this table cannot outlive the layout it describes. AZAZAEL_SRC was declared speculatively on the first run and reported stale; it was removed rather than left in as noise, which is the mechanism working.

2026-10-31 ml_platforms -> ORCHESTRATION.choice: a reference written as `ml_platforms/<file>` resolves to the ORCHESTRATION copy, not HYDRA's
evidence: `ml_platforms` was a repo-root directory before the move; its module path from src is `ORCHESTRATION.ml_platforms`, which is also where the launchers' `ml_platforms\x.py` form resolves
no python module imports either copy (measured: 0 inbound on all six files), so import evidence cannot break the tie
ORCHESTRATION/ml_platforms/health_monitor.py is 18,576 bytes against HYDRA's 1,767: HYDRA's is a stub of the same name, not the implementation
a bare `harness.py` next to a driver additionally resolves by the `nearest` rule, so HYDRA/run_hydra.bat still lands on HYDRA/ml_platforms/harness.py
2026-10-31 ml_platforms -> ORCHESTRATION.reversible: delete the prefix to restore ambiguity; `stale_alias` will flag it if the directory moves again

2026-10-31 nearest tie-break.choice: when a bare name matches more than one file, accept the unique candidate under the referring script's own directory; otherwise stay ambiguous
evidence: a bare `harness.py` beside a launcher means that launcher's copy -- the same directory agreement `tail` establishes, measured from the other end
`nearest` is a resolution labelled separately in resolved_by, so it can be counted, audited, or abolished without touching `tail`

deliberately_absent.AZAZAEL_INTEGRATION.py: no such file anywhere in the tree: a launcher bug, not a resolution gap
deliberately_absent.BIBL/bibl.py: the directory exists, the file is bibl_crawler.py: a launcher bug
deliberately_absent.METAWORMS/HYDROMETA.py: HYDRAMETA.py exists, HYDROMETA.py does not: a spelling bug in the launcher
